prose.philosophical_reflection: The principal dynamic is epithumia (irrational desire) lodged at the horme (impulse) stage — the impulse to write the error claim into the P1 findings memo is already in motion, and the engine identifies that reputation and wealth, both preferred indifferents ranked by axia (worth/value), are being treated as genuine goods rather than as what they are. This is a single snapshot; no trajectory data is available to assess your direction of travel. The classification of this impulse as genuine boulesis (rational wishing) — wanting what virtue would have you want, without grasping — versus epithumia cannot be confirmed from this instance alone. The work is to carry forward the correct judgement: the defect in the production configuration is an external, and your genuine good lies in the quality of your judgement and the integrity of your reporting, not in the recognition or outcome that follows.
prose.improvement_guidance: The false judgement to correct is the assumption that there is genuine good in the external outcome — the fix being adopted, the defect being credited to your discovery, the billing configuration being corrected. Replace it with the corrected judgement that externals are indifferent, and the genuine good is virtue alone, exercised through right judgement, just impulse, and stable character. This is a horme-stage correction: the impulse is already running, so the move is to examine it before it becomes praxis (action) and ask what is actually driving it — the role obligation to report accurately, or the pull toward recognition and outcome. Notice whether the claim you are about to write would be exactly the same if no one would ever know you discovered it; if it would, the impulse is well-grounded. Phronesis (practical wisdom), dikaiosyne (justice), and sophrosyne (temperance) are all engaged here — the virtuous move is to write the claim because it is accurate and the role demands it, not because the outcome is preferred. Practise this now: before you write the claim, name what you are acting from — role obligation or craving — and let the former carry the action.
